preamble: Denasalization of [ĩ] to oral [i]. In Middle French, vowels that had been nasalized before a nasal consonant lost their nasality when that consonant remained syllable-initial (before a vowel), so Old French fine [ˈfĩnə] became [fin], while in closed syllables the nasal vowel survived and lowered (fin [fɛ̃]).

examples.note: Middle French denasalization before /n/ or /m/ followed by a vowel; the same process gave femme [fam] from Old French [ˈfãmə].

sources: Wikipedia contributors. Phonological history of French. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_French
